SK9025 The requested load mode produced no compilation, so a fallback was used

The load mode tried first produced no compilation or could not run, and the next mode on the ladder was used instead: binlog -> workspace -> loose, or workspace -> loose. Info; the report's load summary says which mode actually ran. Name the mode with --load= to make its failure fatal instead of falling back.

CategoryTool
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since0.6

Why

Falling back is the right default for a tool an agent runs unattended, and it is also how a run comes to be measured under a mode nobody chose: a binlog run that quietly became a loose one has no analyzer references and no generated sources, and every semantic rule answers a different question. So the fall is announced, naming the mode that fell, so that a surprising result can be traced to the mode that produced it.

When it does not fire

--load=loose never falls anywhere — asking for loose is asking for speed — so a loose run that finds nothing reports SK9023 and not this. A named mode that fails on its first rung does not fall back; it exits 4. When every rung fails the summary reads nothing could be loaded and the run exits 4.
